$comment: ⭐ THE SEALED GRANT LIST. Read by scripts/check-sealed-grants.mjs (gate 25).
A privilege listed here MUST NOT be granted to the listed role by ANY .sql
file in this repository. The gate fails the build if it finds one, naming
WHY THIS EXISTS: 0012_phase20_secops.sql refused EXECUTE on
prune_security_events() to ordence_app in a comment sitting inside the
files later, in a list of thirty otherwise-correct signatures copied from
the modules that declare them. Every neighbour on that list is granted to
ordence_app by its own module; this one is granted to ordence_maintenance.
The signature was copied, the role was not read, and the line was
indistinguishable from its neighbours for four waves.
A comment cannot enforce anything. This file can.
TO ADD A SEAL: add an entry. TO REMOVE ONE: you are removing a security
control, so say why in `unsealedBecause` and expect it in review.

seals.why: SECURITY DEFINER, and the only sanctioned way past the append-only trigger on security_events. Any role that can execute it can erase the record of its own compromise, whatever its table privileges say.
SECURITY DEFINER retention on metering counters, which are the evidence behind every invoice. The tenant-facing tier must not be able to delete what it is billed on.
The table is append-only evidence. The trigger refuses DELETE, but a trigger can be dropped by a later migration and a missing privilege cannot be bypassed by dropping anything.
UPDATE has no legitimate path at all on security evidence. Amending an event is indistinguishable from erasing it.
The audit log is the record of who did what. A tier that can delete from it cannot be audited.
Row-level security is the ONLY tenant isolation in this product. A role with BYPASSRLS sees every tenant's data on every query and nothing in the application layer would notice.
A superuser bypasses RLS implicitly. Same consequence as BYPASSRLS, reached by a different word.

SECURITY DEFINER and it CREATEs triggers, which requires table ownership. A role that can call it can attach an arbitrary AFTER trigger to any tenant table, executing under the owner's rights on every write.
